subject: Oceanography
title: Ocean Renewable Energy
description: A quick, practical guide to Ocean Renewable Energy.

hook.text: The ocean holds enough energy in waves, tides, and temperature differences to power civilization—if we can harness it.

buildup.text: Offshore wind farms already generate significant power—and wave and tidal energy technologies are maturing.

discovery.text: The Rance tidal barrage in France has generated electricity since 1966—proving the concept for over 50 years.

twist.text: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) uses the temperature difference between surface and deep water to generate power.

climax.text: Floating offshore wind could access vast resources far from shore—where winds are stronger and steadier.

punchline.text: The ocean is an untapped power plant—we just need the right tools.

quiz.question: What does OTEC use to generate electricity?
options: Temperature difference between surface and deep water
